mainTopic: Who איוב was, when he lived, and the opening story of ספר איוב
overview: The גמרא first rereads a ברייתא to say that איוב lived as long as Israel's stay in מצרים, not during that exact time. Two ברייתות then suggest that איוב was not Jewish. The first is a list of seven prophets to the nations, and it is pushed off: those on the list mainly prophesied to the nations, even if they were Jewish. The second ברייתא calls איוב a חסיד among the nations. The גמרא answers that this is a dispute among תנאים. It brings a ברייתא with five opinions on when איוב lived, ranging from יעקב's time to אחשורוש's. Every opinion except the last one dates him after משה, so they must hold that he was Jewish, since after משה the שכינה no longer rested on the nations. רבי יוחנן and others then explain related phrases: the immoral generation, the generation that judged its judges, and מלכת שבא. Finally, the גמרא explains the opening scene of ספר איוב: the שטן's praise of אברהם, ה׳'s greater praise of איוב, and the special blessings on איוב's money and livestock. רבי יוחנן's explanation of the oxen and donkeys continues on the next amud.

steps.title: איוב's lifespan matched the length of the Egypt period
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: איוב lived as long as the time span from Israel's entry into מצרים until the יציאה. It does not say he lived during that exact time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it means: his life lasted as long as from the time Israel entered Egypt until the time they left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a problem by reading the ברייתא about איוב in a new way. The ברייתא is giving the length of his life, not the dates when he lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the ברייתא seemed to place איוב in the years Israel was in מצרים, which clashed with another opinion about when he lived. The answer turns a statement about time period into a statement about length of life. That removes the clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / read it as. Used to offer a new way of understanding a text.
As long as from the time. Here it describes a length of time.

phrases.english: Say: as long as from the time Israel entered Egypt,
until [the time] that they left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised just before this section, about the ברייתא dating איוב to the Egypt period.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא places איוב's life during the years of the Egypt period.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only says his life was as long as that period.

steps.title: Challenge from the list of seven prophets to the nations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists seven prophets who prophesied to the nations of the world, and איוב is among them. This suggests he was not Jewish.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Seven prophets prophesied to the nations of the world. They are בלעם and his father, איוב, אליפז the Temanite, בלדד the Shuhite, צופר the Naamathite, and אליהוא son of ברכאל the Buzite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that איוב was Jewish. A ברייתא puts him on a list of prophets to the nations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption behind the challenge is that a prophet to the nations must himself be from the nations. Since איוב appears together with בלעם and others, he seems to be a non-Jew. That would contradict the opinion that he was Jewish.

phrases.english: They challenged: Seven prophets
prophesied to the nations of the world –
and these are they: Balaam, and his father, and Job,
Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite,
and Zophar the Naamathite,
and Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the view that איוב was Jewish.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that איוב was Jewish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: איוב is listed among prophets to the nations, so he seems to be from the nations himself.

steps.title: Counter-question: אליהוא was Jewish yet is on the list
steps.stepSummary: The answer turns the logic around. אליהוא is on the same list, yet a פסוק shows he came from a Jewish family. So the list cannot prove someone was a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By your reasoning, was אליהוא son of ברכאל not from Israel? But it is written, 'of the family of רם'!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is pushed back with a counter-question. Another name on the same list was clearly Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being on the list meant being a non-Jew, then אליהוא would have to be a non-Jew too. But the פסוק links him to the family of רם, which shows he was Jewish. So the challenger's assumption breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning. Turns the challenger's own logic against him.

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: אֱלִיהוּא בֶן בַּרַכְאֵל – לָאו מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הֲוָה?
phrases.english: Elihu son of Barachel – was he not from Israel?
But it is written: "Of the family of Ram"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 2 by showing its logic fails for אליהוא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that being on the list means being a non-Jew
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אליהוא is on the list but was Jewish according to the פסוק.

steps.title: The list means they prophesied to the nations, even if they were Jewish
steps.stepSummary: The list only says these men prophesied to the nations. They could still be Jewish, like אליהוא, and the same can be said about איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he prophesied to the nations of the world. So too איוב: he prophesied to the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of the list. It tells us who these prophets spoke to, not where they came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אליהוא must be explained this way, איוב can be explained the same way. So the ברייתא no longer shows that איוב was a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: He certainly prophesied. The verb is doubled for emphasis.

phrases.english: Rather, he prophesied to the nations of the world;
so too Job –
he prophesied [to the nations of the world].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the counter-question to give the real meaning of the list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being on the list means being a non-Jew.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being on the list means prophesying to the nations. A Jew like איוב can be included.

steps.title: Didn't all prophets prophesy to the nations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: other prophets also spoke to the nations, so why are only these seven listed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did all the other prophets not prophesy to the nations of the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation. Many Jewish prophets gave prophecies about other nations too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the list only means 'prophesied to the nations,' it should include many more names. Limiting it to seven needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? Introduces a question meant to show a claim cannot be right.

phrases.english: Is it so that all the prophets
did not prophesy to the nations of the world?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the list means 'prophesied to the nations'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Many other prophets also prophesied to the nations, so a list of only seven makes no sense.

steps.title: These seven mainly prophesied to the nations
steps.stepSummary: Other prophets mainly prophesied to Israel. These seven mainly prophesied to the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, their main prophecy was to Israel. Here, their main prophecy was to the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by looking at the main audience of each prophet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is about the main focus of a prophet's message. Most נביאים spoke mostly to Israel, with some words for the nations. These seven spoke mostly to the nations. So איוב can be Jewish and still belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here. Used to contrast two cases.

steps.whatToRemember: Being on the list of 'seven prophets to the nations' describes who a prophet mainly spoke to, not his own nation. So this ברייתא does not prove that איוב was a non-Jew.

phrases.english: There – their main prophecy was to Israel,
phrases.notes: "There" means all the other prophets; "here" means the seven on the list.

phrases.english: here – their main prophecy was to the nations of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any prophet who spoke to the nations should be on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only prophets whose main prophecy was to the nations are listed.

steps.title: Challenge: איוב was a חסיד among the nations
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says plainly that איוב was a חסיד among the nations. When he suffered he cursed, so הקב"ה doubled his reward in this world to remove him from עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: There was a pious man among the nations of the world named איוב. He came into the world only to receive his reward. הקב"ה brought sufferings on him, and he began to curse and blaspheme. הקב"ה doubled his reward in this world in order to drive him out of עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger challenge. This ברייתא says directly that איוב was from the nations. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first list, this ברייתא does not just say whom איוב spoke to. It calls him a חסיד 'among the nations,' which sounds like a direct statement that he was a non-Jew. This directly contradicts the view that איוב was Jewish.

keyTerms.meaning: To drive him out / expel him

steps.confusionAlert: The next step answers this challenge. Do not treat this ברייתא as the final halacha about איוב.

phrases.english: They challenged: There was a pious man among the nations of the world –
and his name was Job,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בָּא לָעוֹלָם אֶלָּא כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל שְׂכָרוֹ.
phrases.english: and he came into the world only to receive his reward.

phrases.aramaic: הֵבִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עָלָיו יִסּוּרִין –
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, brought sufferings upon him –
he began to curse and blaspheme.

phrases.aramaic: כָּפַל לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׂכָרוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, doubled his reward in this world,
[in order] to drive him out of the World to Come!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a new ברייתא brings a more direct challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that איוב was Jewish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls איוב a חסיד 'among the nations,' which says outright that he was a non-Jew.

steps.title: It is a dispute among the תנאים, and רבי אלעזר places איוב in the time of the Judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that whether איוב was Jewish is a dispute among תנאים. It brings a ברייתא, starting with רבי אלעזר, who says איוב lived when the people judged their judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute among the תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר says איוב lived in the days when the Judges were judged. The פסוק says, "Behold, all of you have seen it; why then have you become altogether vain?" Which generation was completely vain? It must be the generation when the Judges were judged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ברייתא from step 7 by saying other תנאים disagree about איוב. It starts quoting a new ברייתא, beginning with רבי אלעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7's ברייתא called איוב a non-Jew. The גמרא does not deny that. It says this is only one side of a dispute among תנאים. רבי אלעזר links the word הבל (vanity) in ספר איוב to a generation known for being empty and corrupt: the time of the שופטים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among the תנאים (the Sages of the משנה era)
The judging of the Judges, a time when the people judged their own leaders
You must say, it can only be

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about WHEN איוב lived. The גמרא will only explain at the end (steps 14 and 15) how these dates tell us whether he was Jewish.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tannaim.
phrases.notes: This answers step 7: the ברייתא there says איוב was a non-Jew, but that's just one opinion.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
Job lived in the days of the judging of the Judges,
as it is stated: "Behold, all of you have seen it,
why then have you become altogether vain?"
Which generation was entirely vain?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל שְׁפוֹט הַשּׁוֹפְטִים.
phrases.english: You must say: this is the generation of the judging of the Judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 7 by showing it is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא in step 7 settles that איוב was a non-Jew.
steps.terutzMaskana: That ברייתא is only one opinion. Other תנאים hold differently.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה: איוב lived in the time of אחשורוש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says איוב lived in the time of אחשורוש, because the פסוק praises איוב's daughters as the most beautiful in all the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: איוב lived in the days of אחשורוש. The פסוק says, "No women were found as beautiful as the daughters of איוב in all the land." In which generation did people go looking for beautiful women? It must be the generation of אחשורוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second opinion. רבי יהושע בן קרחה dates איוב to the time of אחשורוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "no women were found" suggest that someone was searching for beautiful women. The famous search for beautiful women happened under אחשורוש, in the story of אסתר. So רבי יהושע בן קרחה places איוב in that generation.

keyTerms.meaning: The Persian king in מגילת אסתר

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
Job lived in the days of Ahasuerus,
as it is stated: "And no women were found so beautiful
as the daughters of Job in all the land."

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזֶהוּ דּוֹר שֶׁנִּתְבַּקְּשׁוּ בּוֹ נָשִׁים יָפוֹת?
phrases.english: In which generation were beautiful women sought?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ.
phrases.english: You must say: this is the generation of Ahasuerus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב lived in the time of אחשורוש, based on the search for beautiful women.

steps.title: Why not the time of דוד, when they also searched for a beautiful girl?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן קרחה: there was also a search for a beautiful girl in the days of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say איוב lived in the days of דוד? It is written there: "And they searched for a beautiful girl"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יהושע בן קרחה's proof. Another generation also had a search for a beautiful woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה said that only אחשורוש's generation searched for beautiful women. But near the end of דוד's life, they also searched for a beautiful girl. So the proof does not seem to point only to אחשורוש.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us say, why not say

phrases.english: But say it was in the days of David,
as it is written: "And they sought a beautiful girl"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן קרחה's proof that only אחשורוש's generation searched for beautiful women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There was also a search for a beautiful girl in דוד's time, so the פסוק could just as easily point to that generation.

steps.title: דוד's search was only in Israel, but איוב's daughters were the most beautiful in the whole land
steps.stepSummary: In דוד's time the search was only within the borders of ישראל. The פסוק about איוב says "in all the land," which matches אחשורוש's search across his whole kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they searched "throughout the borders of ישראל." Here, it says "in all the land."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהושע בן קרחה by pointing out a difference between the two searches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in מלכים says the search was "in all the borders of ישראל," which is a limited area. The פסוק in איוב says "in all the land," meaning everywhere. That wide search fits אחשורוש, who searched across his whole empire, not דוד.

phrases.english: There, it was throughout the territory of Israel,
phrases.notes: These are the next words in the same פסוק about דוד (מלכים א 1:3).

phrases.english: here, it was in all the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the wording of the פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any search for a beautiful woman could fit, including the one in דוד's time.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a search across the whole world fits איוב's פסוק, and that is אחשורוש's search.

steps.title: רבי נתן says the kingdom of שבא; the חכמים say the time of the כשדים
steps.stepSummary: Two more opinions in the ברייתא. רבי נתן says איוב lived in the time of the kingdom of שבא. The חכמים say he lived in the time of the כשדים. Each bases his view on a פסוק about the raiders who attacked איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: איוב lived in the days of the kingdom of שבא, as it says, "And שבא attacked and took them." The חכמים say: איוב lived in the days of the כשדים, as it says, "The כשדים formed three groups."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a third and a fourth opinion about when איוב lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions use the story at the start of ספר איוב, where raiders steal his animals. רבי נתן says this was when שבא was a powerful kingdom. The חכמים say it was when the כשדים (Babylonians) were powerful.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
Job lived in the days of the kingdom of Sheba,
as it is stated: "And Sheba fell upon them and took them."
And the Sages say:
Job lived in the days of the Chaldeans,
as it is stated: "The Chaldeans formed three bands."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: אִיּוֹב בִּימֵי מַלְכוּת שְׁבָא הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues listing the opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נתן: איוב lived in the time of the kingdom of שבא. חכמים: איוב lived in the time of the כשדים.

steps.title: Some say איוב lived in the time of יעקב and married דינה
steps.stepSummary: A last opinion in the ברייתא says איוב lived in the time of יעקב and married דינה. The proof is the word נבלה, which appears both in ספר איוב and in the story of דינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: איוב lived in the days of יעקב and married דינה, the daughter of יעקב. Here it is written: "You speak as one of the disgraceful women speaks," and there it is written: "For he did a disgraceful act in ישראל."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its fifth and final opinion, which places איוב very early, in the days of יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב calls his wife's words נבלות. The same word, נבלה, describes what was done to דינה. Linking the two פסוקים through this shared word teaches that איוב's wife was דינה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here, and it is written there: linking two פסוקים by a shared word

phrases.english: And some say:
Job lived in the days of Jacob,
and he married Dinah, the daughter of Jacob.
It is written here:
"You speak as one of the disgraceful women speaks,"
phrases.notes: איוב 2:10. איוב is saying this to his wife.

phrases.english: and it is written there: "For he did a disgraceful act in Israel."
phrases.notes: בראשית 34:7, from the story of דינה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אִיּוֹב בִּימֵי יַעֲקֹב הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב lived in the time of יעקב and married דינה.

steps.title: All these opinions hold that איוב was Jewish, except the last one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up: every תנא in the ברייתא holds that איוב was from ישראל, except for the יש אומרים opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: All these תנאים hold that איוב was from ישראל, except for the opinion of "some say."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it brought this ברייתא. Most of these opinions show that איוב was Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we see how the dates connect to step 8's answer. Only the יש אומרים, who place איוב in יעקב's time, would call him a non-Jew. That is the side of the dispute that step 7's ברייתא follows. All the other opinions hold he was Jewish.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold, they are of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: Whether איוב was Jewish is a dispute among the תנאים. Most hold that he was. Only the opinion that places him in יעקב's time holds that he was not.

phrases.english: And all these tannaim hold
that Job was from Israel,
except for "some say."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ תַּנָּאֵי סְבִירָא לְהוּ דְּאִיּוֹב מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from all the opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every opinion except יש אומרים holds that איוב was Jewish.

steps.title: Proof: after משה, the שכינה did not rest on non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that the later opinions must hold איוב was Jewish. After משה died, the שכינה no longer rested on the nations, because משה asked for this and his request was granted.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think איוב was from the nations of the world, then after משה died, does the שכינה rest on the nations? But the Master said: משה asked that the שכינה not rest on the nations of the world, and God granted it to him, as it says: "So that I and Your people will be set apart."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why every opinion that dates איוב after משה must hold that he was Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב received prophecy, which means the שכינה rested on him. After משה's request, the שכינה no longer rested on non-Jews. So anyone who says איוב lived after משה (the שופטים, אחשורוש, שבא, or the כשדים) must hold that איוב was Jewish.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind, if you were to think
The nations of the world, non-Jews
And we will be set apart, made distinct

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a date can decide a person's identity. Prophecy after משה belongs only to ישראל, so dating איוב after משה tells us he was Jewish.

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind
that he was from the nations of the world,
after Moses died,
phrases.notes: All the opinions except יש אומרים place איוב after משה's time.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שָׁרְיָא שְׁכִינָה עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם?
phrases.english: does the Divine Presence rest on the nations of the world?
But didn't the Master say:

phrases.aramaic: בִּקֵּשׁ מֹשֶׁה שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: Moses requested that the Divine Presence not rest on the nations of the world,
and He granted it to him,
as it is stated: "That we shall be set apart, I and Your people."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in step 14 that most of the תנאים hold איוב was Jewish.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that every opinion dating איוב after משה holds that he was Jewish.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that משה asked that the שכינה not rest on the nations, and God agreed (שמות 33:16).

steps.title: The generation of איוב was full of immorality
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says איוב's generation was steeped in immorality. He proves it by linking the word חזיתם in איוב to ונחזה in שיר השירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: איוב's generation was flooded with immorality. The פסוק says, 'You have all seen (חזיתם) it; why then are you so empty?' Another פסוק uses the same word for gazing at a woman: 'Return, return, O שולמית, that we may gaze (ונחזה) at you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us what kind of people lived in איוב's time. He proves it by matching one word that shows up in two different פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The root חזה appears in איוב's words to his generation and also in שיר השירים, where it means looking at a woman. So רבי יוחנן reads איוב's words as criticizing his generation for improper looking.

keyTerms.meaning: You have seen (from the root חזה)
The Shulamite, the maiden of שיר השירים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל אִיּוֹב שָׁטוּף בְּזִמָּה הָיָה,
phrases.english: The generation of Job was awash in immorality,
as it is said: "Behold, all of you have seen it,
so why have you become so empty?"
And it is written: "Return, return, O Shulamite,
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 7:1. Watch for the shared word חזה in both פסוקים.

phrases.english: return, return, that we may gaze at you."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל אִיּוֹב שָׁטוּף בְּזִמָּה הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who איוב was to a description of the people of his generation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב's generation was immoral, shown by the word חזיתם, which means improper gazing as in ונחזה בך.

steps.title: Maybe חזיתם means prophecy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: חזה can also mean a prophetic vision, as in חזון ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means prophecy, as it is written: 'The vision (חזון) of ישעיהו son of אמוץ.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's proof. The same word could mean seeing a prophecy, not improper looking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חזה can mean prophecy, then איוב's words might be praise ('you all saw prophecy') and not criticism. That would knock out the proof that his generation was immoral.

phrases.english: Say it refers to prophecy,
as it is written: "The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word-meaning that רבי יוחנן's proof rests on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of חזיתם as improper gazing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The root חזה is also used for prophecy, so the word does not have to mean immorality.

steps.title: The rest of the פסוק shows it is criticism
steps.stepSummary: If it meant prophecy, the words 'why are you so empty' would make no sense. So the פסוק must be criticizing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need 'why have you become so empty'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by looking at the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק is a rebuke, calling them empty. That fits a sinful generation, not one that saw prophecy, so the reading of חזיתם as improper gazing stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (this part would be pointless)

phrases.english: If so,
why do I need "why have you become so empty"?
phrases.notes: He means: the rebuke only fits if they were doing something wrong.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, ״לָמָּה זֶּה הֶבֶל תֶּהְבָּלוּ״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and restores רבי יוחנן's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Context of the same פסוק decides the meaning
steps.terutzMaskana: The rebuke at the end of the פסוק shows חזיתם means sinful gazing.

steps.title: A generation that judged its judges
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains 'in the days when the judges judged' as a generation that turned around and judged its own judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן also said: What does 'It was in the days when the judges judged' mean? It was a generation that judged its judges. If the judge said, 'Remove the splinter from between your eyes,' the person answered, 'Remove the beam from between your eyes.' If the judge said, 'Your silver has become dross,' he answered, 'Your wine is mixed with water.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains a פסוק in רות to describe the generation of the שופטים. This is one of the time periods suggested for איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double wording 'judging of the judges' is read as the people judging the judges. Every time a judge pointed out a sin, the accused pointed out a bigger sin of the judge. So no one could be corrected.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'judging' is done by the people against their judges, not the other way around. The judges lost their authority because they had the same faults.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said,
What is meant by what is written: "And it was in the days when the judges judged"?
A generation that judges its judges;
if the judge says to him: "Remove the splinter from between your eyes" –
he says to him: "Remove the beam from between your eyes."
If the judge says to him: "Your silver has become dross" –
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:22. Both sides of the argument are quoted from that פסוק.

phrases.english: he says to him: "Your wine is mixed with water."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי בִּימֵי שְׁפוֹט הַשּׁוֹפְטִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי יוחנן, about another generation connected to the question of when איוב lived.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The generation of the שופטים judged its judges, answering every rebuke by pointing to the judge's own sins.

steps.title: מלכת שבא means the kingdom of שבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says it is a mistake to think מלכת שבא was a woman. It means the kingdom of שבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Anyone who says מלכת שבא was a woman is simply mistaken. What does מלכת שבא mean? The kingdom of שבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן reads the words מלכת שבא in a new way. They refer to a kingdom, not a queen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מלכת is read as מלכותא, 'kingdom.' This connects to רבי נתן's opinion from step 12 that איוב lived in the time of the kingdom of שבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Usually read as 'the queen of שבא'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר מַלְכַּת שְׁבָא אִשָּׁה הָיְתָה –
phrases.english: Anyone who says that the queen of Sheba was a woman –
is nothing but mistaken;
What is "malkat Sheba"?
The kingdom of Sheba.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר מַלְכַּת שְׁבָא אִשָּׁה הָיְתָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another short teaching linked to the opinions about איוב's time, here the kingdom of שבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלכת שבא means the kingdom of שבא, not a queen.

steps.title: The פסוק: the שטן comes before ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening scene of ספר איוב, where the שטן appears before ה׳ and is asked where he came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It was the day when the angels came to stand before ה׳, and the שטן also came among them. ה׳ said to the שטן: Where are you coming from? And the שטן answered,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new section. It quotes the פסוק it is about to explain, and the explanation comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the גמרא turns to the story inside ספר איוב itself. The question 'where are you coming from' opens the door to the שטן's answer, which the גמרא will expand on.

phrases.english: "Now it was the day,

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּבֹאוּ בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים לְהִתְיַצֵּב עַל ה׳,
phrases.english: when the sons of God came to stand before the Lord,
and the Satan also came among them.

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֶל הַשָּׂטָן: מֵאַיִן תָּבֹא?
phrases.english: And the Lord said to the Satan: From where do you come?
And the Satan answered, etc." –

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם, וַיָּבֹאוּ בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים לְהִתְיַצֵּב עַל ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that explains the story of ספר איוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the פסוק to be explained: the שטן comes before ה׳ and is asked where he came from.

steps.title: The שטן praises אברהם's faithfulness
steps.stepSummary: The שטן says he searched the whole world and found no one as faithful as אברהם. Even with no burial place for שרה, אברהם did not question ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שטן said before Him: Master of the world, I roamed the whole world and did not find anyone as faithful as Your servant אברהם. You told him, 'Get up, walk the land, its length and its width, for I will give it to you.' Even so, when he had no place to bury שרה until he bought one for four hundred silver shekels, he did not question Your ways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in what the שטן said when he answered ה׳. He praises אברהם as the most faithful person he found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ promised אברהם the whole land, yet he had to pay a lot of money just for a grave for שרה. He still did not complain, and that shows real faithfulness. This sets the stage for comparing איוב to אברהם.

keyTerms.meaning: I roamed (a play on the word שטן)
He did not question Your ways

steps.whyThisMatters: אברהם's quiet trust after a promise seemed unfulfilled becomes the measuring stick for the test of איוב that follows.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
I have roamed through the entire world,
and I have not found anyone as faithful as Your servant Abraham –
to whom You said: "Arise, walk through the land
in its length and its breadth, for to you I will give it,"
and even so,

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁלֹּא מָצָא מָקוֹם לִקְבּוֹר אֶת שָׂרָה
phrases.english: when he did not find a place to bury Sarah
[until he bought one for four hundred silver shekels] –
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: he did not question Your ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, שַׁטְתִּי בְּכׇל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the שטן's answer from the פסוק quoted in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן found no one as faithful as אברהם, who did not question ה׳ even when he had to buy a grave in the land promised to him.

steps.title: איוב's praise is greater than אברהם's
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ praises איוב to the שטן. רבי יוחנן says the פסוק about איוב says more than the one about אברהם, because איוב is also called 'one who turns away from evil.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ said to the שטן: 'Have you noticed My servant איוב? There is no one like him on earth.' רבי יוחנן said: What the תורה says about איוב is greater than what it says about אברהם. About אברהם it only says 'you fear God.' About איוב it says 'a perfect and upright man, who fears God and turns away from evil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the opening of ספר איוב and now reaches ה׳'s praise of איוב. רבי יוחנן compares that praise to the praise of אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אברהם and איוב are called יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים, someone who fears God. איוב also gets extra descriptions: תָּם, יָשָׁר, and וְסָר מֵרָע. Because איוב's list is longer, רבי יוחנן says the praise of איוב is greater.

keyTerms.meaning: Job, the main figure of ספר איוב
The Satan, the accuser in the heavenly court
Whole and upright, a person of complete integrity

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying איוב was a greater person than אברהם in every way. He is only comparing the wording of the two פסוקים.

phrases.english: "And the Lord said to the Satan:
Have you set your heart upon My servant Job,
that there is none like him on earth, etc."
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Greater is what is said about Job
than what is said about Abraham;
for about Abraham it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה״,
phrases.english: "For now I know that you fear God,"
while about Job it is written:
"A perfect and upright man, who fears God [and turns away from evil]."
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets finish the פסוק. They matter because the next step asks what they mean.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּדוֹל הַנֶּאֱמָר בְּאִיּוֹב יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאַבְרָהָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the scene from ספר איוב. The שטן praised אברהם, and now ה׳ points to איוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק's praise of איוב is greater than the praise of אברהם, because איוב is given more descriptions.

steps.title: What does 'turns away from evil' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra phrase 'turns away from evil' adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'and turns away from evil'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the extra phrase in איוב's praise. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This phrase is part of what made רבי יוחנן say איוב's praise is greater. So the גמרא wants to know what actual behavior it describes.

phrases.english: What is "and turns away from evil"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the key phrase from the פסוק quoted in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical behavior 'turning away from evil' describes in איוב.

steps.title: איוב gave up small sums owed to him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר שמואל explains that איוב was generous with his money. He let customers keep the half-פרוטה they owed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר שמואל said: איוב was easygoing with his money. Normally, a person pays the storekeeper even half a פרוטה. איוב would let it go and absorb the loss himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר שמואל answers the question. 'Turning away from evil' means איוב was generous and did not insist on tiny amounts owed to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most people expect to be paid every coin they are owed, even a tiny half-פרוטה. איוב waived these small debts. This shows he stayed far from anything close to greed or unfairness with money.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who gives in or lets things go, especially with money
The normal way of the world

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Shmuel said:
Job was forgiving with his money.
The way of the world is that
one gives half a peruta to the storekeeper;
Job would forgive it from his own.
phrases.notes: When איוב was the storekeeper owed that half-פרוטה, he let the customer off and took the loss himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Turns away from evil' means איוב waived even tiny amounts owed to him.

steps.title: The שטן's reply and the meaning of 'You blessed his work'
steps.stepSummary: The שטן answers that איוב only fears God because ה׳ protects and blesses him. The גמרא asks what 'You blessed the work of his hands' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שטן answered ה׳: 'Does איוב fear God for nothing? Haven't You put a fence around him and his house?' The גמרא asks: what is meant by 'You blessed the work of his hands'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the שטן's response to ה׳ and then asks about one phrase in it. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטן claims איוב's goodness is only because he is protected and blessed. One of the blessings he lists is 'the work of his hands.' The גמרא wants to know what was special about that blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: For nothing? Without getting anything back?
You put a fence of protection around him

phrases.english: "And the Satan answered the Lord and said:
Does Job fear God for nothing?!
Have You not made a hedge around him
and around his house, etc."
phrases.notes: איוב 1:9–10. The 'etc.' includes the phrases the גמרא asks about next.

phrases.english: What is "You have blessed the work of his hands"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק, the שטן's answer to ה׳'s praise in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was special about the blessing on איוב's handiwork.

steps.title: Anyone who took a פרוטה from איוב was blessed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק explains that the blessing reached beyond איוב. Anyone who received even a פרוטה from him was blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: Anyone who took a פרוטה from איוב became blessed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק answers the question. The blessing on איוב's work was so strong that it spread to anyone who got money from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain reading would be that איוב's own business succeeded. This answer adds that the blessing passed on to others, even through a tiny coin.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
Anyone who took a peruta from Job was blessed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing on איוב's work passed on to anyone who received even a פרוטה from him.

steps.title: What does 'his livestock broke out' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the next phrase in the שטן's words: 'and his livestock increased in the land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'and his livestock spread out (פָּרַץ) in the land'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another phrase from the same פסוק. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פָּרַץ can mean 'increased,' but it also means 'broke through.' The גמרא is opening the door to a reading based on that second meaning.

phrases.english: What is "and his livestock increased in the land"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק from Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word פרץ means when said about איוב's livestock.

steps.title: איוב's goats killed wolves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that איוב's livestock broke the normal order of nature. His goats killed wolves instead of being killed by them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: איוב's livestock broke through the fence of the world's normal order. Normally wolves kill goats. With איוב's livestock, goats killed the wolves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא reads פָּרַץ as 'broke through.' איוב's animals broke the normal rules of nature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reading פָּרַץ as 'multiplied,' he reads it as פָּרְצוּ גִּדְרוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, breaking the boundary of nature. The example is that איוב's goats overpowered wolves. This shows how far ה׳'s protection of איוב went, which is exactly the שטן's point.

keyTerms.meaning: The fence, or normal order, of the world

steps.whatToRemember: Each phrase of praise in the opening of ספר איוב is read as more than ordinary success. He waived even half a פרוטה, anyone who took a פרוטה from him was blessed, and his goats defeated wolves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: מִקְנֵהוּ שֶׁל אִיּוֹב פָּרְצוּ גִּדְרוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם;
phrases.english: Job's livestock broke through the fence of the world;
the way of the world is that
wolves kill the goats,
but with Job's livestock,
goats killed the wolves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְנֵהוּ שֶׁל אִיּוֹב פָּרְצוּ גִּדְרוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פָּרַץ means איוב's livestock broke the natural order: his goats killed wolves.

steps.title: The שטן gets permission, and the גמרא asks about the oxen and donkeys
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוקים where the שטן asks to strike איוב's possessions, ה׳ agrees, and a messenger reports that the oxen were plowing and the donkeys grazing beside them. The גמרא then asks what that description means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But now put forth Your hand and touch all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face. And ה׳ said to the שטן: Behold, all that he has is in your hand, only upon him do not put forth your hand, etc. And there was a day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother, and a messenger came to איוב and said: The oxen were plowing, etc.' What is meant by 'The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing beside them'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues reading the story of איוב, then stops on one phrase in the messenger's report and asks what it means. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטן claims that if איוב loses everything, he will turn against ה׳. ה׳ allows the שטן to touch איוב's possessions but not איוב himself. The messenger's report includes a detail that seems unnecessary, the donkeys grazing beside the plowing oxen, so the גמרא asks what it comes to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: The accuser, the angel who challenges איוב's righteousness before ה׳
Literally 'he will bless You.' Here it is a polite way of saying 'he will curse You.'
'And so on.' The rest of the פסוק continues.

steps.confusionAlert: The word יְבָרְכֶךָּ literally means 'bless,' but in this פסוק it means the opposite. The text avoids writing 'curse God' directly.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: ה׳ gave איוב a taste
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן begins to explain that the oxen and donkeys phrase teaches that the הקדוש ברוך הוא gave איוב a special 'taste.' The explanation continues in the next lines of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave איוב a taste...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts answering the question about the oxen and donkeys. He says the phrase shows that ה׳ let איוב 'taste' something special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the phrase as a hint about something unusual ה׳ gave איוב, not just a plain farm detail. His sentence is not finished here. What exactly איוב tasted is explained in the next lines, so wait for it before drawing conclusions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It teaches.' This shows a lesson is being drawn from the פסוק.
